title: Trade-history/ledger table + realized-loss-aware 6% Rule
description: The book's actual 6% Rule formula has two parts: realized losses for the current month PLUS risk on currently open trades. `total_open_risk_pct` (backend/app/portfolio/risk.py) only ever implements the second part -- there is no trade-history/ledger model in the schema at all (app/db/models.py has PositionORM/AccountORM/WatchlistItemORM/OHLCVCacheORM, nothing recording a closed position's realized P&L or close date). Concretely: a user who took three straight stopped-out losses earlier this month, then opens a new, individually-fine 2%-sized position, sails right past the 6% Rule today. Add a closed-trade table (ticker, entry/exit price+date, quantity, realized P&L, and an exit-reason tag per Elder's own taxonomy -- target hit / stop hit / reached value zone / going nowhere / starting to turn / couldn't stand the pain / recognized junk trade after entry), populate it when a position closes, and extend the 6% Rule computation to sum this-month's realized losses alongside open-position risk. This table is also the prerequisite for backend-trade-grading and the trade journal frontend task -- design its schema with those in mind even though implementing them is out of scope here.

checklist.step: Design and add the closed-trade ORM table (ticker, quantity, entry/exit price+date, realized P&L, exit-reason tag) to backend/app/db/models.py, with a migration.
Hook position-close (find/confirm the existing delete-position code path in backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py) to record a closed-trade row instead of just deleting state.

Extend the 6% Rule computation (a new function alongside total_open_risk_pct, or an extension of it -- decide and record) to sum this calendar month's realized losses from the new table plus existing open-position risk.
Unit tests covering: a month with prior realized losses that pushes a new, individually-fine position over the 6% threshold; a fresh calendar month correctly excluding the prior month's losses.
Regenerate backend/openapi.json/frontend types if any response shape changed; document in docs/Analyse.md §7.
